sources_considered.why: Controlled experiments vary model size and training amount and document predictable scaling.
Original study documents diminishing returns under data constraints, with an appropriately limited scope.
Recent primary research examines task-dependent saturation but includes contemporary post-training and cannot isolate scaling alone.
Read as foundational context; the later controlled study provides more relevant evidence that the specified regime was attempted.

evidence_items.explanation: The researchers report a controlled testbed varying model size and training tokens, establishing that the scaling regime was attempted. Predictable gains within that testbed also caution against treating scaling as already exhausted.

The study finds saturation when compute is added while repeatedly reusing constrained data. That is evidence of a specific scaling limit, not a demonstration that scaling model size and additional data cannot reach trustworthy general intelligence.

This recent study examines capability boundaries and saturation across benchmarks. Its observational comparisons include contemporary post-training, so they cannot determine the ultimate effect of scaling alone.

unresolved_gaps: No cited result establishes a fundamental ceiling below trustworthy general intelligence.
No qualifying scaling-only demonstration of trustworthy general intelligence was found.
The claim supplies neither an agreed capability threshold nor a deadline.
Observed benchmark saturation and gains do not cleanly isolate all changes besides scale.
